Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.controllers

Class Controller

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.controllers.Controller
Direct Known Subclasses:
SimulatedController, SparkMaxController, TalonFXController, TalonSRXController, VictorSPXController
public abstract class Controller extends Object
Abstract base for a Ninjas motor controller wrapper: a hardware-agnostic API for driving a single motor mechanism (with optional followers) in percent-output, position, or velocity control, and for reading back its encoder position/velocity, current draw, and limit switches. Concrete subclasses wrap a specific vendor API - SparkMaxController (REV SparkMax), TalonFXController (CTRE TalonFX), TalonSRXController (CTRE TalonSRX), VictorSPXController (CTRE VictorSPX) - or run entirely in software via SimulatedController. Subsystems should generally obtain an instance through createController(ControllerType, ControllerConstants) rather than constructing one directly, so the same subsystem code works both on the real robot and in simulation.

  • Constructor Details

    • Controller

      public Controller(RealControllerConstants constants)
      Sets up the state shared by every Controller implementation: allocates a DigitalInput for each non-virtual hard limit, and, if a CANcoder is configured to run in Normal mode, constructs and configures it. Subclasses call this via super(constants) before setting up their own hardware.
      Parameters:
      constants - the controller configuration (base, control, soft/hard limits, CANcoder)

  • Method Details

    • setPercent

      public void setPercent(double percent)
      Switches to open-loop percent-output control. This base implementation only records the new Controller.ControlState; every concrete subclass overrides it to also drive the motor (calling super.setPercent(percent) first).
      Parameters:
      percent - how much to power the motor, between -1 and 1
      See Also:
      • setPosition(double)
      • setVelocity(double)
      • stop()

    • setPosition

      public void setPosition(double position)
      Commands the controller to closed-loop position control. This is the main way to move a mechanism to a specific setpoint (e.g. an elevator height or arm angle); the concrete subclass drives the actual PID/Motion Magic/profile control per its ControllerConstants once this base method records the goal.
      Parameters:
      position - the wanted position, in the units defined by the controller's gear ratio/conversion configuration
      See Also:
      • setPercent(double)
      • setVelocity(double)
      • stop()

    • setVelocity

      public void setVelocity(double velocity)
      Commands the controller to closed-loop velocity control, e.g. for a flywheel or drivetrain wheel spun at a target speed. The concrete subclass drives the actual PID/feedforward once this base method records the goal.
      Parameters:
      velocity - the wanted velocity, in the units defined by the controller's gear ratio/conversion configuration, per second
      See Also:
      • setPercent(double)
      • setPosition(double)
      • stop()

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops all motor movement by switching back to percent-output control at zero. Concrete subclasses override this to also command the hardware to stop.
      See Also:
      • setPercent(double)
      • setPosition(double)
      • setVelocity(double)

      public abstract double getPosition()
      The primary encoder reading every position-based subsystem call relies on. The value is in the units defined by the concrete implementation's gear ratio/conversion configuration (typically rotations of the mechanism, not the motor).

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Runs the controller's periodic bookkeeping - call this from the owning subsystem's periodic() every loop. On a real robot this debounces each configured limit (real switches by reading the DigitalInput, virtual limits by watching stator current against RealControllerConstants.HardLimits.HardLimit.virtualStallThreshold while within its position window) and, once a limit becomes newly active, invokes its RealControllerConstants.HardLimits.HardLimit.limitTriggerMethod if enabled.

    • resetVirtualLimit

      public void resetVirtualLimit(int index)
      Clears the "was previously at limit" flag for one virtual limit, e.g. after intentionally driving off of it, so it doesn't immediately re-trigger.
      Parameters:
      index - the index of the limit in RealControllerConstants.HardLimits.limits

    • resetVirtualLimits

      public void resetVirtualLimits()
      Clears the "was previously at limit" flag for every configured limit.

    • createController

      public static Controller createController(Controller.ControllerType type, ControllerConstants constants)
      Factory method that builds the right Controller implementation for the given Controller.ControllerType: a real hardware wrapper when running on the robot (RobotBase.isReal()), or a SimulatedController when running in simulation. This is the preferred way to construct a controller so subsystem code doesn't need to branch on real-vs-simulated itself.
      Parameters:
      type - which hardware (or simulation) to create
      constants - the controller configuration
      Returns:
      a new controller instance appropriate for the current robot mode

    • getLogs

      public Controller.ControllerLogs getLogs()
      Snapshots the controller's current state into a loggable, struct-serializable Controller.ControllerLogs record (position, velocity, acceleration, output, currents, goal, limit switches, etc.) - intended to be called once per loop and logged/published for telemetry (e.g. via AdvantageKit or NetworkTables).
      Returns:
      a new Controller.ControllerLogs populated with this controller's current values
